newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni H1 net profit seen lower.
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni H1 net profit seen lower.

text.p: Czech Komercni Banka a.s. will post first half net profits of around two billion crowns, according to Czech accounting standards, on Thursday, down from 2.57 billion crowns last time, a Reuters poll of analysts on Wednesday said.
The analysts said that Komercni's profits according to to international accounting standards (IAS) were seen between 1.8 and 2.4 billion after 3.06 billion crowns previously.

Pavel Sobisek, chief analyst at Zivnostenska Banka, said this year's figures would be adversly affected by the sharp fall in bond prices in May and June in the wake of central bank efforts to defend the crown by tightening monetary policy.

"(Komercni) bank overvalued its bonds. I assume that this will show itself in the portfolio as a fall of around 750 million crowns and that is about the sum by which profits will also fall," said Sobisek.
Some analysts also said that the results would be lower because of a greater need to create reserves for risky loans.
"What will be negative will be the decline in payment willingness (of companies)," said Libor Knappek of Brno Broker Group.
Komercni's share price closed up 25 crowns to 1,660 on the main market of the Prague bourse on Wednesday.
But the shares are down 27.85 percent since the beginning of the year and have underperformed a falling PX50 index by 23.9 percent.
